title: Streaming JSON delimiter synthesis, backpressure & truncate-consensus for toolcall resilience
creator: Aisha Chen
description: We continue to see class of failures when model output is streamed and truncated mid-JSON object during tool/function calls. Current heuristics (bracket counting + escape scanning) handle common cases but fail on nested arrays, multi-byte token boundaries, and when clients intentionally backpressure. This ticket designs and implements a robust "truncate-consensus" + delimiter-synthesis approach that: (1) synthesizes safe closing delimiters when safe to do so, (2) produces an idempotent resume token that encodes KV-cache offsets and a checksum for deterministic resume, (3) defines a light-weight backpressure header to avoid frequent truncations, and (4) follows security constraints for resume tokens via KMS-backed HMAC signing. Goal: reduce tool-call failures caused by truncated structured output by >= 90% in Canary and provide a safe opt-in for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Delimiter synthesis recovers valid JSON for >90% of simulated truncations in fuzz harness (nested depth up to 10, arrays and objects).
Resume token includes request-id, kv-cache-offset, and 64-bit checksum; HMAC-signed using KMS key; server rejects mismatched checksum when resuming.
No regression in median token latency >2ms and p99 latency increase <10ms for streaming requests in Canary cluster.
Client and server interop tests pass for the new backpressure header and resume flow across SDKs (python/js).
Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 feature-flag and opt-in customer setting for Private installs.
implementation_notes: Introduce a small per-chunk manifest appended as metadata every N tokens (configurable, default N=256) containing: chunk-index, bracket-balance delta, L2 checksum of bytes. Manifest uses compact JSON+base64 and is stripped for customers that opt-out.

Truncate-consensus algorithm: run heuristics in priority order - manifest consensus -> bracket-balance repair -> token-alignment check -> last-resort delimiter-synthesis by placing matching closing brackets and null-terminator for trailing primitives.

Delimiter synthesis must avoid creating ambiguity for tool-call parsers: synthesized delimiters are marked by a reserved 'synth' field in the resume token and never persisted in logs unless customer enables synthetic-marker redaction.
Resume token format: base64(HMAC(KMS_key, request_id || '|' || kv_offset || '|' || chunk_index || '|' || checksum || '|' || synth_flag)). Use AES-GCM for optional encryption for Private installs.
Backpressure header: x-rw-window: <tokens> where client indicates remaining token budget. Server uses this to decide flush/hold. If header absent, server uses conservative default 64 tokens.
Opt-in flags: runtime.feature.streaming_truncate_consensus=true and customer.config.allow_resume_tokens must be enabled for resume tokens to be issued.
Security: rotate HMAC keys via KMS rotation policy; resume tokens expire after 15 minutes; logs redact resume token payload except checksum and request-id.
Rollout: start with internal Canary (10% of traffic), expand to hosted customers with opt-in, then include as default for Dedicated/Private after security review.
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Spike completed exploring manifest size tradeoffs; 24-byte manifest (index+balance+checksum) looks sufficient in practice. Recorded throughput overhead ~0.7% on synthetic workload.

2025-02-17: Prototype implemented in streaming runtime (branch feat/stream-truncate-consensus). Added unit tests for bracket-balance repair and token alignment. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789.

2025-02-18: Security reviewed resume-token design with Security team; principal concerns: token leakage and KMS usage. Agreed to HMAC+optional AES-GCM and 15m expiry. Follow-up: add automated log-redaction (ENG-80701).
2025-02-20: Began SDK compatibility changes (python SDK: add resume_from_token + x-rw-window header). Internals team to validate p99 latency impact in Canary next week.
testing_plan: Fuzz harness that truncates streams at random byte offsets (1K inputs, depths up to 10) and verifies resulting JSON validity after server-side repair.
Integration tests that simulate KV-cache drift: resume token with stale kv_offset must be rejected and client receives clear retryable error code (429/RESUME_MISMATCH).
Performance benchmark against the streaming baseline to measure median/p99 latency and throughput impact with manifest enabled and disabled.
Interoperability tests between python/js SDKs and runtime with explicit backpressure header behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal Canary): enable feature-flag for 5 internal services; monitor tool-call failure rate and latency for 7 days.
Phase 2 (hosted opt-in): expose opt-in toggle in Console for hosted customers; enable for beta customers and gather feedback.
Phase 3 (Dedicated/Private): require security sign-off and customer opt-in for resume tokens; provide migration guide for on-prem installs.
Phase 4 (GA default): enable server-side repair by default for new runtime-1.22 deployments if no security concerns remain.

Security (2025-02-18): Approved HMAC+15min expiry approach but require a short design doc for AES-GCM option for Private installs.
